A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text and Appendices A-C. Their equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v5 reports original reasoning, decision-tree in-context-learning, and WikiText-103 experiments in Tables 2-4, plus an edit-distance analysis in Appendix C.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments and the appendix analysis, with revised WikiText-103 results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The timestep embeddings, conditioning network, time-dependent RMSNorm, and residual scaling remain unchanged. Section 4.2 renames the architecture; the language-modeling size changes are experimental configurations rather than a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Sudoku, Countdown, longest common subsequence, edit distance, decision-tree in-context learning, and WikiText-103. The represented tasks, datasets, and input-length scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2-4 retain the same comparison methods: standard Transformers, ordinary Looped Transformers, and timestep-conditioned Looped Transformers. The additional related-work citations are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported language-modeling protocol is substantially revised: Table 4 changes loop counts from 6 to 24, while Appendix C changes the looped model from 16 heads and dimension 2048 to 12 heads and dimension 768, batch size from 64 to 48, and optimizer/scheduling settings. The baseline depth remains ambiguous because v6's Table 4 says 12 layers while Appendix C.3 says 6.

E4.justification: Figure 5 retains the same edit-distance training/test-accuracy analysis across loop counts, moved from Appendix C.2 to C.1.2. No new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis is added; the highlighted 100-loop result already appears in v5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The tables and Figure 5 retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces the WikiText-103 results: standard/looped/timestep-conditioned test perplexities change from 19.6/28.2/22.4 to 20.5/20.6/19.6, and training perplexities from 5.11/5.61/5.05 to 15.9/17.1/15.9. The best test model changes from standard to timestep-conditioned Transformer, but these are different settings, not same-setting gains. Tables 2-3 and Figure 5 retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the inconsistent discretization condition from δ ≥ 2 to δ^(-1) ≥ 2. The principal approximation, universality, and memorization results and their constructions remain intact. The shortened bit-complexity bound is asymptotically equivalent to v5's expression.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain approximation-rate analysis using three continuity moduli, identification of a looped-architecture limitation, and timestep conditioning to address it. The introduction's explicit fixed-length continuous-function qualification matches the scope already used in v5's theory.

C2.justification: The conclusion revises the stated open problems: v5 emphasizes lower bounds and function classes avoiding dimensionality dependence; v6 instead adds multilayer extensions, optimal memorization capacity, estimation performance, and training stability. The interpretation of timestep conditioning and the existing experimental trends is retained.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a code-repository link. Appendix C.3 adds explicit baseline dimensions, a parameter-matching rationale, block size 1024, and language-modeling-specific optimizer and scheduling details. These disclosures improve specificity, although baseline-depth and batch-size descriptions are internally inconsistent.

R1.justification: v6 adds discussion and citations for Bai et al., Barron, Csordás et al., and Wang and E, including a new Wang and E row in Table 1. It also clarifies the distinction from Saunshi et al. concerning fixed parameter counts. The overall research positioning remains the same.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, proof explanations, and conclusion receive localized rewrites. Section 4.2 is renamed, 'selector' becomes 'impulse,' and Appendix C is reorganized by task. The main section sequence and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with colored markers, a legend, and revised axes and labels while illustrating the same interpolation argument. Table 1 gains a row, and headers, equation numbering, and appendix placement change. Figures 1, 3, 4, and 5 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, the corrected discretization condition, redrawn Figure 2, and added code/configuration information provide benefits. However, the principal experimental revision is inconsistently documented: Table 4 specifies a 12-layer baseline while Appendix C.3 specifies 6, and the retained general training paragraph gives batch size 64 where C.3 gives 48. These conflicts undermine reproducibility of the replacement language-modeling results, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
